naming: A "name" is the keyword as written in a program, except where one keyword covers two unrelated features that fall in different scopes. Those carry a parenthetical qualifier — "GET (graphics)" and "GET (file)", "PUT (graphics)" and "PUT (file)" — so each scope decision has its own entry. The qualifier is an editorial disambiguator, not part of the keyword: a lookup by keyword name must match on the text before the space and parenthesis, and will find more than one entry for GET and PUT. PAINT carried such a split until 2026-08-17, when spec.md §3.3 widened to bring tile patterns into scope; with both halves in scope the split had nothing left to record, and PAINT is one entry again.

kinds.statement: a complete, self-contained BASIC statement or command
kinds.function: an expression-valued built-in, called by name in an expression
kinds.function-statement: usable both as a function in an expression and as a statement (an assignment target, or read/write like a pseudo-variable)
kinds.clause: a keyword that only ever appears inside another statement (e.g. THEN/ELSE inside IF), never on its own
kinds.type-suffix: a character suffixed to an identifier or literal to fix its numeric/string type
kinds.comment: the marker introducing a line comment
kinds.option: a suffix modifying another statement's form, not a keyword usable on its own (LINE's ,B and ,BF)
kinds.device: a device name referenced from I/O statements, not itself a statement or function
